p: Croydon has some lively spots to round off a trampoline session. Boxpark Croydon, right by East Croydon station, is a buzzing food and drink venue built from shipping containers, with a range of street food stalls that should keep even the fussiest eater happy. It's a fun, relaxed place for a post-bounce feed.

If you'd rather get outside, Lloyd Park is a big green space with room to run, and Addington Hills nearby has a viewing platform with sweeping views across London. On a clear day, you can spot landmarks right across the city skyline.

A short trip north takes you to Crystal Palace Park, famous for its Victorian dinosaur sculptures, which have been delighting kids for over a century and a half. It's a great add-on for families with young dino fans.

Back at Oxygen, a little preparation helps the session run smoothly. Sort the waiver form online before you leave, wear sporty clothes and bring a water bottle. Sessions are usually about an hour, which is plenty for most kids, as trampolining is surprisingly tiring.

If you're bringing a mixed-age group, check whether there are sessions geared towards younger children, which tend to be calmer and less crowded. Parents who don't want to join in can watch from the side, though it's always more fun to have a go.
Fairfield Halls, Croydon's revamped arts venue, is worth a look if you fancy a show in the evening to round off the day.
